summary: Source-anchored research for Data type selection for storage. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Choose a type whose range covers expected values and whose precision preserves the application's meaning. PostgreSQL documents integer as the common balance of range, storage size, and performance; it describes smallint as useful when disk space is at a premium and bigint as appropriate when integer range is insufficient. PostgreSQL integer widths are 2, 4, and 8 bytes for smallint, integer, and bigint. (high confidence)

At the BSON value-encoding level, Int32 uses 4 bytes, Int64 and Double use 8 bytes, and Decimal128 uses 16 bytes. A MongoDB community reply notes that Decimal128 is twice as big as an int64, so field values are larger in an uncompressed format such as the WiredTiger cache. Collection data on disk is block-compressed by default, so value size alone does not determine on-disk size. Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/bsonspec.org/blob/master/spec.html ; https://developer.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/data-type-for-migration-from-oracle-to-mongodb/103214 ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/faq/storage/

For MongoDB decimal workloads, Decimal128 supports exact decimal values, while a scale-factor model stores values as a 64-bit integer after multiplying by a power of ten. The integer model requires that the scale be chosen so the needed precision becomes the integer's least significant digit and that applications scale values consistently; MongoDB documents Decimal128 as preferred over the scale-factor method for monetary data. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/tutorial/model-monetary-data/

Use an exact decimal type when decimal precision must be preserved, such as for monetary values. The MongoDB Decimal128 specification says BSON Double is insufficient for some values that require strict decimal rounding; PostgreSQL recommends numeric for money and other exact quantities, while warning that numeric calculations are slower than integer or floating-point calculations. (high confidence) Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/bson-decimal128/decimal128.md ; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype-numeric.html

When decimal values need exact storage or arithmetic, select an exact decimal type instead of binary floating point. PostgreSQL says to use numeric when exact storage and calculations are required, notes numeric calculations are very slow compared to integer and floating-point types, and lists numeric storage as variable; MySQL describes DECIMAL and NUMERIC as types that store exact numeric data values. Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype-numeric.html ; https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E17952_01/mysql-8.4-en/fixed-point-types.html

For MongoDB time-series collections, rounding numeric measurements to the precision the application requires can improve the compression ratio. Preserve any precision the application needs. (low confidence)

In PostgreSQL, row alignment can add padding between columns, so declared field widths alone do not determine total row size. Column order affects padding. Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/15/catalog-pg-type.html ; https://docs.gitlab.com/development/database/ordering_table_columns/

For bounded whole-number fields, choose a width that covers the full valid range and expected growth. PostgreSQL documents 2-, 4-, and 8-byte smallint, integer, and bigint types with different ranges; MySQL documents 1-, 2-, 3-, 4-, and 8-byte integer types with signed and unsigned ranges. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-21) Sources: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype-numeric.html ; https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E17952_01/mysql-8.4-en/integer-types.html

Inference: nominal type widths do not always translate into proportional whole-table savings. MySQL states that storage-engine layout and compression affect on-disk size; its NDB engine aligns values to four bytes, so TINYINT, SMALLINT, MEDIUMINT, and INT each use four bytes per record there. Estimate savings against the target engine's physical layout. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-15)
